item.title: Arson, crude bombs put Bangladesh on alert as state turns stricter
item.description:
The government no longer wants to act only after a crime has occurred. This time, it wants to build resistance before one takes place.
In response to the law and order situation arising from crude bomb explosions on the streets, arson attacks on vehicles, attacks on police stations and government installations, and organised violence in different parts of the country, the government's strategy is changing. Rather than relying solely on arrests or deploying additional forces, emphasis is being placed on identifying those who plan and finance sabotage, as well as criminals operating on the ground, and bringing them under the law.
Recent directives from the prime minister, the home minister and the Inspector General of Police (IGP) have made the government's firm stance clear. However, how effective this firmness will be depends on advance intelligence, coordinated efforts among the forces, and the ability to bring actual offenders to justice without harassing innocent people.
According to those concerned, the government now faces two major challenges in light of recent incidents.
The first is controlling sabotage and violence centred around political programmes and restoring a sense of relief to public life.
The second is building effective resistance against extortion, terrorism, mugging, drugs, juvenile gangs and organised crime. They also believe that if the government's tough stance remains limited to suppressing political violence, the long-term crisis in public safety will not be resolved.
Since the beginning of November, a series of sabotage incidents in different parts of the country, including the capital, has called into question the capabilities of law enforcement agencies.
In some places passenger buses have been set on fire, and in others railway tracks. Elsewhere, crude bomb attacks have targeted police stations, police vehicles and important government installations.
The attacks, vandalism and arson at the Tungipara and Muksudpur police stations in Gopalganj have made the situation more complicated.
Meanwhile, the Awami League, a party whose activities are banned, has announced protest marches, torch processions and a lockdown from November 22 to November 30.
Police Headquarters AIG (Media) Kamarum Munira said that from November 7 to 19, crude bomb explosions occurred at 87 locations across the country, and 83 incidents of arson involving transport vehicles took place.
In addition, 4 police installations were subjected to arson and vandalism, as were 28 vehicles. Crude bomb explosions occurred at 3 installations, and 1 vehicle was damaged by a crude bomb explosion.
A total of 39 cases have been filed and 66 people arrested in connection with these incidents.
Dhaka Metropolitan Detective Police chief and Additional Commissioner Shafiqul Islam said the number of crude bomb explosions increased significantly in the first 20 days of November compared with September and October.
Additional law enforcement personnel have been deployed in the capital and several vulnerable districts. Checkpoints have been set up and surveillance of suspicious activities has been increased.
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has instructed the administration and law enforcement agencies to take strict and timely measures to prevent attempts to create instability in the country.
At a cabinet meeting at the Secretariat on November 15, the overall law and order situation and the security of the ready-made garment industry were discussed.
The prime minister instructed that prompt legal action be taken if attempts are made to engage in violence, sabotage or disruption of public safety under the cover of political activities. He also stressed the responsible role of ministers, state ministers and public representatives in maintaining normal conditions in their electoral areas.
Earlier, addressing the police, he had said: "You are people of the law, not of any particular party. Legal action must be taken without considering a criminal's political identity or influential position."
He also emphasised the importance of the police earning public trust, not harassing innocent people and ensuring humane behaviour.
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has repeatedly spoken about taking strict legal measures over the recent sabotage and violence.
On November 9, responding to journalists at the Secretariat, he alleged that the ousted political force was trying to create instability in the country. On the identity of those carrying out sabotage, he said: "Whoever they are, they are miscreants."
On November 17, speaking in parliament about the attack and arson at the Tungipara police station, he said: "The attackers will be identified by reviewing video footage, photographs and audio recordings. No one involved will be spared."
He also spoke of taking legal measures instead of using indiscriminate force, and of ensuring the safety of innocent people. Earlier, he had said that the law and order situation was under control across the country and that law enforcement agencies were determined to prevent any kind of sabotage and terrorism.
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Md Ali Hossain Fakir has instructed field-level officials to take strict measures to prevent sabotage.
At a meeting at Police Headquarters on November 10, he discussed the situation with the superintendents of police of the country's 64 districts, range DIGs and metropolitan police commissioners. Instructions were given to identify and arrest the actual criminals involved in setting vehicles on fire, crude bomb explosions and attacks on the police.
Emphasis was also placed on strengthening intelligence activities to identify those planning sabotage, financing it and carrying out attacks at the field level. Officials were warned to ensure that innocent people are not harassed in the name of operations.
On November 20, the IGP, SRB Director General Faruk Ahmed and BGB Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui inspected the situation in Gopalganj on the ground. Coordinated activity by law enforcement agencies received importance during the visit.
Asked on Friday (November 20) whether the force would become stricter in dealing with sabotage, the IGP said: "Everything necessary will be done in accordance with the law and the Constitution."
He called on peace-loving local people to take a stand against those creating disorder and to cooperate with the police. At a meeting with police officials of the district the same day, he emphasised identifying those involved in sabotage, collecting intelligence and taking strategic measures based on the situation.
From this position, it can be understood that although strictness in the force's field-level activities is increasing, efforts are being made to prioritise information-based operations instead of indiscriminate arrests or excessive use of force.
To control the overall situation, coordinated activity involving the Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB), the Special Response Battalion (SRB) and other forces has been increased alongside the police.
On Saturday (November 21), the force's Public Relations Officer Md Shariful Islam gave details of BGB deployments in Dhaka, Narayanganj, Gazipur, Gopalganj, Mymensingh, Faridpur and Cox's Bazar.
He said 90 platoons of BGB have been deployed in different districts, including the capital, to control law and order and ensure public safety. Of these, 18 platoons are in Dhaka district, 5 in Dhaka metropolitan area, 6 in Narayanganj, 15 in Gazipur, 29 in Gopalganj, 2 in Mymensingh, 5 in Faridpur and 6 in Cox's Bazar. In addition, 4 platoons have been kept ready for deployment.
BGB personnel, deployed on the instructions of the Ministry of Home Affairs, will work in coordination with the district administrations and other law enforcement agencies. Alongside strengthening security and surveillance at important installations, industrial areas and other key locations, they will act to prevent any kind of disorder, violence and activities that pose a threat to public safety.
Technology-based surveillance from the monitoring cell at BGB Headquarters is continuing. Live footage from drones, body-worn cameras and other modern technologies is being monitored round the clock.
Md Nazmus Sakib, Assistant Director of the Public Relations Department at the Bangladesh Ansar and Village Defence Force headquarters, said on Saturday (November 21) that 49 platoons of Ansar personnel are currently on duty in seven districts. Of these, 15 are in Gopalganj, 13 in Gazipur, 5 in Faridpur, and 4 each in Narayanganj, Khulna, Madaripur and Shariatpur.
Preparations have also been made to deploy another 4 platoons in Satkhira and Mymensingh, bringing the total of deployed and planned personnel to 53 platoons.
He said security has been strengthened at important government installations, prisons, roads and public gathering places in different districts, including Gopalganj. Patrols and surveillance are continuing in the industrial areas of Gazipur and Narayanganj to ensure workers return to their workplaces, factory production remains operational and traffic movement remains normal.
Although the situation is calm in several areas, Ansar personnel remain on alert amid concerns over workers' protests, work stoppages and road blockades. They are working in coordination with the local administration and relevant forces to ensure public safety and a normal working environment.
Wing Commander M Z M Entekhab Chowdhury, Director of the Legal and Media Wing of SRB, told Dhaka Tribune: "If anyone attempts to carry out any violence, SRB will do whatever is necessary under the law to prevent it."
He said a joint team comprising members of the SRB-6 and SRB-10 battalions is on duty in Gopalganj.
AIG (Media) Kamarum Munira said measures have been taken to collect advance intelligence information, increase patrols, set up checkpoints and ensure a rapid response to maintain a normal law and order situation.
In the capital, night patrols and supervision by senior officials have been strengthened on the instructions of DMP Commissioner Mosleh Uddin Ahmed. Md Akhtar Hossain, Deputy Commissioner of the DMP Media and Public Relations Division, said checkpoints and police activities have increased during both day and night.
Gazipur Metropolitan Police Commissioner Md Ashik Saeed said sabotage and anarchy will not be tolerated under any circumstances. He has instructed subordinate officials to take preventive measures.
Statistics on regular and special police operations in the capital also show an increase in activity. According to DMP information, its report on November 19 stated that 537 people had been arrested in the previous 24 hours. Its report on November 20 stated that 474 people had been arrested, and its report on November 21 stated that 299.
However, not all of these arrests were related to the recent sabotage. Arrests in connection with regular crime prevention activities and various cases are also included in these statistics.
Crime analyst Md Tawohidul Haque believes that alongside arresting people carrying crude bombs or setting vehicles on fire, it is essential to identify the locations where explosives are made, the supply routes, the sources of funding and those issuing instructions.
In this regard, he said, CCTV footage, mobile phone data, digital communications and forensic evidence must be used effectively.
He also said it is necessary to increase the capacity to submit charge sheets quickly, based on information obtained through investigations, and to present evidence in court. Increasing the number of arrests alone, he said, cannot ensure long-term success in controlling crime.
